questions.question: What exact demand did the 70 chosen men of Bani Israel make upon arriving at Mount Tur?
options: اذْهَبْ أَنْتَ وَرَبُّكَ فَقَاتِلَا — Go, you and your Lord, and fight
لَن نُّؤْمِنَ لَكَ حَتَّىٰ نَرَى اللَّهَ جَهْرَةً — We will never believe in you until we see Allah openly
لَنْ نَصْبِرَ عَلَىٰ طَعَامٍ وَاحِدٍ — We will not endure one kind of food
أَرِنَا اللَّهَ جَهْرَةً بَعْدَ الِاسْتِغْفَارِ — Show us Allah openly after we seek forgiveness
questions.explanation: They said: 'We will never believe in you until we see Allah openly (جَهْرَةً).' They had already heard Allah's speech but refused to accept it as sufficient.

questions.question: What did Allah state was the purpose of resurrecting the 70 men after they were struck down at Tur?
options: لَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ — that you may be grateful
لَعَلَّكُمْ تَهْتَدُونَ — that you may be guided
لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ — that you may be mindful of Allah
لَعَلَّكُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ — that you may reason
questions.explanation: Allah revived the 70 after a full day and night, stating the purpose: لَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ — 'that you may be grateful.'

questions.question: What strange experience did Bani Israel have while wandering in the Tih during their 40-year punishment?
options: The sun would not set for them, depriving them of rest
They could hear voices calling them but could never find the source
They walked all morning but found themselves back at the starting point by evening
They would forget the path they had just walked and had to start over each day
questions.explanation: Despite walking all morning to cross the field, they would find themselves back at the starting point by evening — unable to exit the Tih.

questions.question: What was الْمَنُّ (al-Mann), one of the three blessings Allah provided to Bani Israel in the Tih?
options: A honey-like liquid that descended onto tree leaves, mixed with water and drunk
A sweet bread that fell from the sky each morning without effort
A quail-like bird of exceptional flavor sent down for food
Fresh water that sprang from twelve rocks at Musa's command
questions.explanation: Al-Mann was a honey-like liquid that descended upon the leaves of trees. Bani Israel mixed it with water and drank it — pure divine provision requiring no labor.

questions.question: What punishment followed when the wrongdoers among Bani Israel substituted the word حِطَّة with a mocking phrase?
options: Shade was removed from them and the intense desert heat returned
They were struck by a thunderbolt like the 70 men at Tur
They were condemned to wander the Tih for another 40 years
A plague (طَاعُون) that killed 70,000 in a single hour
questions.explanation: The wrongdoers substituted حِطَّة with a mocking phrase and entered on their backsides instead of prostrating. The punishment was a plague (طَاعُون) that killed 70,000 in a single hour.

questions.question: According to Ayah 62, which four religious communities does the verse address regarding its conditions for reward?
options: Muslims, Jews (الَّذِينَ هَادُوا), Christians (نَصَارَى), and Sabians (صَابِئُون)
Muslims, Jews, Christians, and Zoroastrians (Majūs)
Believers, hypocrites (Munāfiqūn), Jews, and Christians
Arabs, Jews, Christians, and pagans (Mushrikūn)
questions.explanation: The four communities addressed are: Muslims (followers of Muhammad ﷺ), Jews (الَّذِينَ هَادُوا), Christians (نَصَارَى), and Sabians (صَابِئُون).

questions.question: Which of the following is one of the two patterns of تَأَجُّب (expressing wonder/astonishment) in Arabic?
options: أَفْعَلُ التَّفْضِيلِ — e.g., أَكْرَمُ (more honourable)
مَفْعُولٌ — e.g., مُكَرَّمٌ (one who is honoured)
فَعَّالٌ — e.g., كَرِيمٌ (a very honourable person)
أَفْعِلْ بِهِ — e.g., أَكْرِمْ بِهِ (How honourable he is!)
questions.explanation: One of the two تَأَجُّب patterns is أَفْعِلْ بِهِ (e.g., أَكْرِمْ بِهِ, 'How honourable he is!'). The other pattern is مَا أَفْعَلَهُ (e.g., مَا أَكْرَمَهُ).

questions.question: What does جَهْرَةً mean in the context of Bani Israel's demand at Mount Tur?
options: Temporarily, for a short time
Secretly, in a hidden manner
Willingly, with full consent
Openly, manifestly
questions.explanation: جَهْرَةً means openly, manifestly — Bani Israel demanded to see Allah directly and openly, as opposed to merely hearing His speech.

questions.question: What does the root verb of تِيه (tāha yatīhu) mean, making this name fitting for the place of Bani Israel's punishment?
options: To be lost in darkness
To be confined under punishment
To circle in fear
To wander aimlessly
questions.explanation: تِيه comes from تَاهَ يَتِيهُ, meaning to wander aimlessly. The name fits because Bani Israel literally wandered without being able to leave, making it 'the field of aimless wandering.'

questions.question: How did Bani Israel consume الْمَنُّ (al-Mann) that was sent down for them in the Tih?
options: They spread it over السَّلْوَى as a flavoring
They ate it directly off the leaves of trees
They mixed it with water and drank it
They cooked it into a type of sweet bread
questions.explanation: Al-Mann was a honey-like liquid that descended upon tree leaves. Bani Israel mixed it with water and drank it, receiving sustenance without effort.

questions.question: What distinguished السَّلْوَى (as-Salwā) from ordinary food of its type?
options: The fact that it arrived already prepared and ready to eat
Its exceptionally delicious taste
Its ability to sustain Bani Israel without need for drink
Its unusually large size compared to normal quail
questions.explanation: السَّلْوَى was a quail-like bird sent as food, distinguished by its delicious taste — described as exceptional in flavor compared to ordinary quail.

questions.question: What did the wrongdoers among Bani Israel say instead of حِطَّة when commanded to seek forgiveness?
options: اذْهَبْ أَنْتَ وَرَبُّكَ فَقَاتِلَا — Go, you and your Lord, and fight
حَبَّةٌ فِي شَعِيرَةٍ (a grain in barley) — a mocking substitution
إِنَّا لَن نُّؤْمِنَ لَكَ — We will never believe you
لَا نَدْخُلُ (we will not enter) — an outright refusal
questions.explanation: The wrongdoers substituted حِطَّة with حَبَّةٌ فِي شَعِيرَةٍ ('a grain in barley') — a meaningless, mocking phrase — as an act of outright ridicule of Allah's command.

questions.question: What nuance does رَغَدًا carry beyond simply meaning 'a lot' or 'abundantly'?
options: Abundance gained only after sustained effort and labor
Enjoying plentiful blessings in a pleasant, carefree manner
Abundance distributed equally and justly among all people
A large surplus stored and reserved for times of scarcity
questions.explanation: رَغَدًا indicates abundance combined with ease and happiness — enjoying plentiful blessings in a pleasant, carefree manner, not merely having a large quantity.

questions.question: Which of the following was one of the three causes that led to ذُلّ (humiliation) and مَسْكَنَة (wretchedness) being permanently imposed on Bani Israel?
options: Abandoning the Torah and replacing it with human rulings
Killing the prophets unjustly and aggressively
Worshipping idols inside the Bayt al-Maqdis
Refusing to pay the obligatory Zakat to those in need
questions.explanation: One of the three causes was killing the prophets unjustly and aggressively. The other two were: disbelieving in Allah's signs out of juḥūd and arrogance, and disobedience ('iṣyān) and transgression (i'tidā').

questions.question: According to the tafseer of Ayah 62, what did the Sabians (الصَّابِئُون) turn to after breaking away from their original religion?
options: Worshipping the stars and celestial bodies
Rejecting all religion and embracing Greek philosophy
Worshipping the angels
Following a distorted form of Christianity
questions.explanation: The Sabians broke away from Judaism and Christianity and began worshipping the angels. They are mentioned three times in the Quran (Al-Baqarah 62, Al-Ma'idah 69, Al-Hajj 17).

questions.question: In Ayah 56, the verb بَعَثَ is used in the context of the 70 men at Tur. Which of its two Quranic meanings applies here?
options: To awaken someone from sleep
To resurrect/revive the dead
To send/dispatch a messenger with a mission
To summon someone before a higher authority
questions.explanation: بَعَثَ has two meanings: (1) to resurrect/revive the dead, and (2) to send/dispatch (e.g., a prophet). In Ayah 56, the context of the 70 men being struck down means it refers to resurrection.

questions.question: Which of the following is the sixth Fard of Salah according to Imam al-Quduri's list of Fara'id?
options: Recitation of Surah al-Fatihah in every rak'ah
Performing Salam at the conclusion of Salah
Al-Qa'dah al-Akhirah for the duration of Tashahud
Ta'deel al-Arkan (stillness between postures)
questions.explanation: The sixth Fard is Al-Qa'dah al-Akhirah for the duration of Tashahud. Salam is sometimes counted as a seventh, but Imam al-Quduri's omission of it will be addressed in a future session.

questions.question: According to Imam Abu Yusuf, which wordings of Takbir al-Tahreemah are valid?
options: Only 'Allahu Akbar' exclusively, with no variation permitted
'Allahu Akbar', 'Allahu Ajall', 'Allahu A'zam', and 'Ar-Rahmanu Akbar'
Any phrase that glorifies or magnifies Allah
Only 'Allahu Akbar' or 'Allahu Kabir' — must contain the root k-b-r
questions.explanation: Imam Abu Yusuf restricts the Takbir to only Allahu Akbar or Allahu Kabir — both must contain the root k-b-r. Imam Abu Hanifah accepts a broader range including Allahu Ajall and Allahu A'zam.

questions.question: What is the minimum amount of Quran required to satisfy the Wajib of adding a Surah after Surah al-Fatihah?
options: Any single meaningful word or phrase from the Quran
At least half of any Surah of the Quran
Three short ayahs OR one long ayah from any Surah
Ten short ayahs OR the entirety of one complete Surah
questions.explanation: The minimum is three short ayahs OR one long ayah from any Surah of the Quran. Because this is Wajib (not Fard), its omission can be compensated by Sajdah Sahu rather than repeating the Salah.

questions.question: What is the ruling on Ta'deel al-Arkan according to the Sahibayn and Imam Shafi'i?
options: Wajib — missing it requires Sajdah Sahu to compensate
Mustahabb — recommended but its omission has no legal consequence
Fard — missing it invalidates the Salah
Sunnah Mu'akkadah — leaving it is disliked but the Salah remains valid
questions.explanation: For the Sahibayn and Imam Shafi'i, Ta'deel al-Arkan is Fard — missing it invalidates the Salah. For the Ahnaf it is Wajib, meaning Sajdah Sahu can compensate.

questions.question: According to Imam Abu Hanifah, what is the ruling on the nose touching the ground during Sajdah?
options: Both the forehead and nose must touch the ground
The nose is Fard while the forehead is Wajib
Only the forehead is required; the nose has no ruling in Sajdah
Either the forehead or the nose touching is sufficient
questions.explanation: Imam Abu Hanifah holds that either the forehead or the nose is sufficient. The Sahibayn (Mufta bihi) require both to touch the ground, and Imam Shafi'i also makes both Fard.

questions.question: Under what condition is Sajdah on a turban (amama) or prayer mat permissible?
options: The forehead must still be able to feel the hardness and make firm contact with the surface
The turban must be made of natural, unprocessed cotton fabric
There must be a valid medical excuse preventing direct contact with the ground
The weather must be so extreme that direct contact with the ground causes harm
questions.explanation: Sajdah on a turban is permissible when the forehead can still feel the hardness of the ground and make firm contact. It becomes impermissible when the cloth is so thick that no contact is made at all.

questions.question: If a Fard pillar is missed mid-Salah but only remembered after the Salah is complete, what must the musalli do?
options: Perform Sajdah Sahu at the end to compensate for the missed pillar
Add an extra rak'ah immediately after the current Salah
Repeat the Salah entirely
Continue with the next Salah and the missed Fard is forgiven
questions.explanation: If a Fard is only remembered after the Salah is complete, the Salah must be repeated entirely. Missing a Fard cannot be compensated by Sajdah Sahu — unlike a missed Wajib.

questions.question: How does missing a وَاجِب intentionally without performing Sajdah Sahu affect the Salah?
options: The Salah is valid but a minor sin is incurred
The Salah is automatically and immediately invalid
The musalli must add an extra rak'ah to compensate
The Salah must be repeated
questions.explanation: If a Wajib is deliberately omitted without Sajdah Sahu, the Salah must be repeated. Missing a Fard, by contrast, automatically invalidates the Salah outright rather than requiring repetition.

questions.question: According to the Ahnaf, which comes first when beginning Salah — raising the hands or saying 'Allahu Akbar'?
options: Raising the hands first, then saying 'Allahu Akbar'
Both are performed simultaneously
Saying 'Allahu Akbar' first, then raising the hands
The order varies depending on whether one is Imam or Muqtadi
questions.explanation: According to the Ahnaf, hands are raised first, then 'Allahu Akbar' is said. The dalil for this sequence is a Hadith in Muslim.

questions.question: تَعْدِيلُ الْأَرْكَان applies at two specific points in each rak'ah — which are they?
options: At the beginning of Qiyam and at the beginning of Ruku
During Tashahud and at the moment of Salam
During Qiyam before Ruku and during Ruku itself
After rising from Ruku (before the first Sajdah) and between the two Sajdahs (the Jalsa)
questions.explanation: Ta'deel al-Arkan applies at two points: (1) standing fully upright after rising from Ruku before going into the first Sajdah, and (2) sitting (the Jalsa) with Itminan between the two Sajdahs.

questions.question: Approximately how many missed Wajibs can one set of سَجْدَةُ السَّهْو compensate for?
options: Any number of missed Wajibs without limit
Up to approximately three
Only one missed Wajib at a time
Up to five missed Wajibs before repetition is required
questions.explanation: One set of Sajdah Sahu can compensate for multiple missed Wajibs, up to approximately three. Beyond a certain number of missed Wajibs the Salah must be repeated (exact limit to be confirmed in a future session).

questions.question: Why is it important to know which position is مُفْتَى بِهِ (Mufta bihi) when the Hanafi Imams differ among themselves?
options: It represents exclusively the view of Imam Abu Hanifah in all cases
It is the position agreed upon by all four major madhabs
It tells the student which position to follow in practice
It indicates the most lenient opinion for ease of the community
questions.explanation: The Mufta bihi is the operative fatwa position acted upon in the school. It tells the student which view to follow in practice, even when other valid scholarly opinions exist within the same school.

questions.question: According to Imam Abu Hanifah, who says سَمِعَ اللَّهُ لِمَنْ حَمِدَهُ when rising from Ruku?
options: The Muqtadi only
Only the person praying alone (Munfarid)
Both the Imam and the Muqtadi
The Imam only
questions.explanation: According to Imam Abu Hanifah (Mufta bihi), only the Imam says سَمِعَ اللَّهُ لِمَنْ حَمِدَهُ. The Muqtadi says رَبَّنَا لَكَ الْحَمْدُ instead and does not say the Tasmi'.

questions.question: What is the minimum duration of اِطْمِئْنَان (stillness) required in the Jalsa between the two Sajdahs?
options: Enough time to say 'Alhamdulillah' two or three times — a genuine, settled pause
The duration required to recite Surah al-Ikhlas once
A momentary touch of any length, however brief, is sufficient
The same duration as the full Tashahud recitation
questions.explanation: The minimum Itminan in the Jalsa is enough time to say 'Alhamdulillah' two or three times — a genuine, settled pause, not a momentary touch and immediate rise.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of Khabar as Jumlah Shartiyya (conditional sentence)?
options: زَيْدٌ قَامَ أَبُوهُ
زَيْدٌ أَبُوهُ قَائِمٌ
زَيْدٌ إِنْ جَاءَنِي فَأَكْرَمْتُهُ
عَمْرٌو فِي الدَّارِ
questions.explanation: زَيْدٌ إِنْ جَاءَنِي فَأَكْرَمْتُهُ is Khabar as Jumlah Shartiyya. The others are: Jumlah Ismiyya (زَيْدٌ أَبُوهُ قَائِمٌ), Jumlah Fi'liyya (زَيْدٌ قَامَ أَبُوهُ), and Zarfiyya/Jar-Majrur (عَمْرٌو فِي الدَّارِ).

questions.question: What must be present inside a Khabar that is a Jumlah, and what is its grammatical function?
options: A Fi'l (verb) that agrees with the Mubtada in gender and number
A Damir (pronoun) referring back to the Mubtada, linking the predicate to the subject
An Ism Zahir (explicit noun) that repeats the Mubtada for clarity
A Harf Nafi that negates the predicate of the sentence
questions.explanation: A Damir referring back to the Mubtada must be present. In زَيْدٌ قَامَ أَبُوهُ, the هُ in أَبُوهُ refers back to زَيْد — without it there would be no logical link between subject and predicate.

questions.question: Which of the following is one of the three conditions required for a Sifat to function as Mubtada?
options: It must be preceded by the definite article (ال)
It must appear at the very end of the sentence
It must agree with the following noun in number and gender
It must come after a Harf Nafi or Harf Istifham (e.g., مَا, هَلْ)
questions.explanation: One of the three conditions is that the Sifat must come after a Harf Nafi or Harf Istifham such as مَا or هَلْ. The other two conditions are: it must be a Sighat Sifat, and it must give Rafa' to the following Ism Zahir.

questions.question: Applying the diagnostic test to مَا قَائِمَانِ الزَّيْدَانِ, what is the grammatical role of قَائِمَانِ?
options: Na'at (adjective) — because it describes the quality of الزَّيْدَانِ
Mubtada — because it appears before the noun in the sentence
Amil — because it stays Wahid (singular) regardless of the noun's number
Khabar — because it matches الزَّيْدَانِ in Tasniyah (dual), indicating agreement
questions.explanation: The diagnostic test: if the Sifat matches the following noun in number, it is Khabar. قَائِمَانِ matches الزَّيْدَانِ in Tasniyah → قَائِمَانِ = Khabar and الزَّيْدَانِ = Mubtada.

questions.question: In the sentence إِنَّ زَيْدًا قَائِمٌ, what is the I'rab of زَيْدًا?
options: Mubtada, Marfoo'
Ism Inna, Mansoob
Fa'il of an implied verb, Marfoo'
Khabar Inna, Marfoo'
questions.explanation: After Inna enters, the Mubtada becomes Ism Inna and takes Nasb (Mansoob). زَيْدًا is the Ism Inna, Mansoob; قَائِمٌ is the Khabar Inna and remains Marfoo'.

questions.question: In an Inna construction, which type of Khabar is permitted to be fronted (Muqaddam) over the Ism Inna?
options: Zarf or Jar-Majrur only — e.g., إِنَّ فِي الدَّارِ زَيْدًا is permitted
Only a Sifat Mushtaq (derived adjective) used as Khabar
No Khabar can ever be fronted in any Inna construction
Any Khabar freely, just as in a regular Mubtada-Khabar sentence
questions.explanation: In an Inna construction, only a Zarf or Jar-Majrur Khabar may be fronted over the Ism Inna. A non-Zarf Khabar (e.g., إِنَّ قَائِمًا زَيْدًا) is not permitted.

questions.question: When Khabar is a Zarf or Jar-Majrur, which Fi'l is described as مَحْذُوف (implied/omitted)?
options: ذَهَبَ — meaning 'to go / to proceed'
كَانَ — meaning 'to be / to exist'
اسْتَقَرَّ — meaning 'to be present / to reside'
وُجِدَ — meaning 'to be found / to exist'
questions.explanation: The implied Fi'l is اسْتَقَرَّ ('to be present/to reside'). The full sentence عَمْرٌو فِي الدَّارِ means عَمْرٌو اسْتَقَرَّ فِي الدَّارِ. Arabic habitually omits it while the meaning remains understood.

questions.question: Why is a Zarf described as مُتَعَلِّق (linked/connected) in Arabic grammar?
options: It requires a Damir (pronoun) to refer back to the subject of the sentence
It is always placed immediately before the Mubtada in the sentence
It cannot stand alone grammatically — it must connect to a Fi'l or its equivalent to complete the predication
It must agree in gender and number with the Mubtada it modifies
questions.explanation: A Zarf is Muta'alliq because it cannot stand alone — it must be connected to a Fi'l or something functioning as a Fi'l (here the implied اسْتَقَرَّ) to complete the predication.

questions.question: What does النَّوَاسِخ mean, and what grammatical effect do they produce on a Mubtada-Khabar sentence?
options: Negators — they reverse the I'rab by making the Khabar Mansoob instead of Marfoo'
Abrogators — they override the default I'rab, changing the Mubtada to Mansoob (with Inna) or altering both elements (with Kāna)
Modifiers — they restrict the meaning of the Khabar to a specific time or place
Connectors — they link multiple Mubtada-Khabar sentences into a compound structure
questions.explanation: النَّوَاسِخ means 'Abrogators.' They enter upon an existing Mubtada-Khabar structure and override its default I'rab — e.g., Inna makes the Mubtada Mansoob while the Khabar stays Marfoo'.

questions.question: Before Inna entered the sentence, what was the grammatical role and I'rab of what becomes the اسم إِنَّ?
options: Fa'il — Marfoo'
Na'at (adjective) following the Mubtada
Khabar — Marfoo'
Mubtada — Marfoo'
questions.explanation: Before Inna entered, this word was the Mubtada (Marfoo'). After Inna enters, it becomes the Ism Inna and shifts to Mansoob. The Khabar retains its original Rafa'.

questions.question: In the sentence مَا قَائِمٌ زَيْدٌ, which word is the عَامِل (Amil) and what grammatical effect does it cause?
options: The sentence has no Amil because مَا negates all grammatical governance
قَائِمٌ — it causes Rafa' in زَيْدٌ, governing it as its Khabar/Fa'il-in-meaning
زَيْدٌ — it governs قَائِمٌ and assigns it Rafa'
مَا — it causes Nasb in the word that immediately follows it
questions.explanation: In مَا قَائِمٌ زَيْدٌ: the Amil is قَائِمٌ (the Sifat acting as Mubtada), and its Ma'mul is زَيْدٌ. The Amil causes Rafa' in زَيْدٌ — it is Marfoo' because قَائِمٌ governs it.

questions.question: Which of the following is one of the four Sighat Sifat that qualify for the Mubtada exception rule?
options: Ism Makan (noun of place)
Ism Zaman (noun of time)
Ism Maf'ul
Ism Alah (noun of instrument)
questions.explanation: The four qualifying Sighat Sifat are: Ism Fa'il, Ism Maf'ul, Sifat Mushabbaha, and Ism Tafdhil. All four are eligible to become Mubtada when the three conditions are met.

questions.question: In the sentence فِي الدَّارِ زَيْدٌ, which element is مُقَدَّم (fronted) and is this arrangement permissible?
options: زَيْدٌ is Muqaddam because it is the known subject while the Khabar follows
Both elements are equally fronted since neither is a pronoun
Neither is Muqaddam — fronting requires a preceding Harf Nafi
فِي الدَّارِ is Muqaddam (fronted Khabar) — this arrangement is Ja'iz (permissible)
questions.explanation: فِي الدَّارِ (the Jar-Majrur) is Muqaddam — the fronted Khabar; زَيْدٌ is Mu'akhkhar — the delayed Mubtada. This arrangement is fully Ja'iz in a regular Mubtada-Khabar sentence.
